get.description:
Returns the current quotes for one item across marketplaces, identified by its Steam market hash name.

- The result has at most one quote per market and side, sorted by `market_code` and then `side`. When several sources report the same market, a quote that is still listed takes precedence over a delisted one, then data taken directly from that marketplace over aggregators, then the most recently confirmed quote (`fresh_at`) wins.
- A market is reported as delisted (`delisted_at` set, `quantity` `0`, last known price kept) only when every source for it has delisted the item.
- Items with enough market data also get one `CSCP` quote with `side` `mid`: the cs.cheap valuation, a weighted consensus of the marketplaces' sell listings and buy orders, refreshed once a day and given in the response `currency`. Its `valuation` object carries the confidence (`credibility`, `uncertainty`) and the two consensus prices; on every other quote `valuation` is `null`. It is an estimate, not a tradable offer.
- Narrow the result with `markets` (comma-separated market codes; `CSCP` selects the valuation) and `side` (`ask`, `bid`, `mid` or `all`).
- `market_hash_name` must match exactly, including case.
- Marketplace prices (`market_price_amount`) are decimal strings in each marketplace's own currency (`market_currency_code`) and are never converted.
- `buy_amount`, `sale_amount` and `payout_amount` say what buying, selling, and selling then withdrawing at that price come to after the marketplace's fees, all in one currency: the `currency` parameter, else your account's base currency, else `USD`. The response's `currency` names it; the `CSCP` quote uses it too.
- `currency` accepts any official currency code (see `GET /currencies`). Any other code — including a base currency that is not supported — is `422 unsupported_currency`, never billed.
- `404` means the item has no quotes at all for this `app_id`. An item whose quotes are all excluded by `markets` or `side` returns `200` with an empty `markets` list.

> [!note]
> This endpoint is billed per request. Failed requests, including `404`, are never charged; `meta.credit` reports the cost and your estimated remaining balance.

post.description:
Returns the current quotes for a list of items in one call, or for every priced item page by page. Each item's quotes follow the same rules as `GET /prices`: at most one per market and side, listed quotes preferred over delisted ones, then marketplace-sourced data over aggregators, then the freshest, plus the item's `CSCP` valuation (`side` `mid`) when it has one.

**With `market_hash_names`** you get exactly the items you name:

- `items` has one entry per requested name, in request order.
- Unknown names are not an error: they come back with an empty `markets` list. This endpoint never returns `404`.
- Duplicate names are kept, and each occurrence gets its own entry.

**Without `market_hash_names`** you page through every item of `app_id` that has a matching quote:

1. Omit `market_hash_names`; `limit` sets the page size (default 100, at most 1000).
2. Pass `meta.page.next_cursor` back unchanged as `cursor` to get the next page.
3. When `next_cursor` is `null`, you have every item.

Items come in the same order as `GET /prices/export`, each at most once per pass. Prices are read as each page is requested, so an item added while you page may only show up on your next pass.

In both modes:

- `markets` and `side` filter every item the same way, and `currency` converts every item as on `GET /prices`.
- Unknown fields in the request body are rejected with `422`.

> [!note]
> Billed per started block of 100 items: the full `market_hash_names` list including duplicates, or the `limit` of a page, even when the last page holds fewer items. To fetch everything at once, `GET /prices/export` is cheaper. The cost is checked before the lookup (`402` if your balance is too low) and charged only when the request succeeds.

get.description:
Downloads the quotes of every priced item of one game as one file, for bulk synchronization. `side` defaults to `ask`; `side=mid` exports only the `CSCP` valuation of every valued item, a much smaller file.

- The body is the export document itself (`app_id`, `side`, `currency`, `generated_at`, `items`), gzip-compressed (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) — not the usual envelope. The request id and the billing fields are response headers instead: `X-Request-ID`, `X-Billable`, and on a billed response `X-Credit-Cost` and `X-Credit-Remaining`.
- `items` lists every item with at least one quote on the requested side, ordered by market hash name; each item's quotes follow the same rules as `GET /prices`.
- The file is a snapshot rebuilt on the server every few minutes; `generated_at` (also the `X-Export-Generated-At` header) says when. Requests in between receive the same file.
- Send the `ETag` you received back as `If-None-Match`: while the snapshot is unchanged the answer is `304 Not Modified` with no body, and a `304` is never billed.
- `currency` picks the file: `USD`, `CNY` or `RUB` (default: your account's base currency, else `USD`). It sets the currency of `buy_amount`, `sale_amount`, `payout_amount` and of the `CSCP` quotes, as on `GET /prices`; any other currency is `422 unsupported_currency`. Each currency is its own file with its own `ETag`.
- `Range` requests are not supported; the whole file is always sent. There is no pagination or market filter.
- `503 dependency_unavailable` means the first snapshot has not been built yet; retry after a minute.

> [!warning]
> Every `200` is billed, even when the file has not changed. Poll with `If-None-Match` and you only pay when there is something new.

Returns the custom currencies you created, with the USD exchange rates you set for them. Official currencies are not included unless you ask for `owner=official`; see also `GET /currencies`.

post.description:
Creates a private currency owned by you, for use in your own convert operators. Nobody else can see it.

- `code` is required; `name` is optional; `kind` defaults to `fiat`.
- `usd_rate` is the value of one unit in US dollars. It is required and must be positive, with at most 12 decimal places (`422` otherwise).
- The new currency is never official, whatever the request contains.

Returns `409` when you already have a live currency with the same `code`. Codes only need to be unique among your own currencies: an official currency with the same code does not conflict, and the code of a deleted currency can be reused.

Requires an active subscription (`403 subscription_required`).

market_code.title: Market Code
market_code.description: Code of the marketplace this quote is for, for example `BUFF`. `CSCP` marks the cs.cheap valuation of the item: a weighted consensus across marketplaces in the response `currency`, refreshed daily, with no quantity, its computation time in `changed_at` and `fresh_at`, and its details in `valuation`. provider_code.description: Code of the source the quote was collected from. Equals `market_code` when the data comes from the marketplace itself; otherwise it names an aggregator reporting that marketplace's prices.

side.description: `ask` for a sell-listing quote, `bid` for a buy-order quote, `mid` for the `CSCP` valuation (the midpoint of the sell and buy consensus).

market_currency_code.title: Market Currency Code
market_currency_code.description: Currency of `market_price_amount`, for example `CNY`. Marketplace prices are returned in the marketplace's own currency, without conversion; only the `CSCP` quote is given in the response `currency`.

market_price_amount.title: Market Price Amount
market_price_amount.description: Price in `market_currency_code` as a decimal string (plain notation, trailing zeros trimmed, never scientific notation), or `null` when the source reports no price. A delisted quote keeps its last known price.

buy_amount.title: Buy Amount
buy_amount.description: What buying at this price actually costs in cash, the marketplace's fees included, converted into the response `currency`, as a decimal string. `null` when the fees are unknown or not yet computed for the current price, and always `null` on the `CSCP` quote.

sale_amount.title: Sale Amount
sale_amount.description: What selling at this price credits to your marketplace balance after the sale fees, converted into the response `currency`, as a decimal string. `null` when the sale fees are unknown, selling there is not supported, or the fees are not yet computed for the current price; always `null` on the `CSCP` quote.

payout_amount.title: Payout Amount
payout_amount.description: What selling at this price leaves you in cash after the sale and withdrawal fees, converted into the response `currency`, as a decimal string. `null` when those fees are unknown, selling or withdrawing there is not supported, or the fees are not yet computed for the current price; always `null` on the `CSCP` quote.

quantity.title: Quantity
quantity.description: Quantity on this side of the market as reported by the source, or `null` when not reported. `0` once the item has been delisted.

is_quantity_minimum.title: Is Quantity Minimum
is_quantity_minimum.description: `true` when `quantity` is a lower bound (the source only reports "at least" this many), or `null` when unknown.

is_all_items_same_price.title: Is All Items Same Price
is_all_items_same_price.description: `true` when every unit on offer is at `market_price_amount`; `false` when the source reports only the best price or the prices differ; `null` when unknown.

changed_at.title: Changed At
changed_at.description: When the price or quantity of this quote last changed at the source, in RFC 3339 UTC (for example `2026-09-24T03:12:08Z`).

observed_at.title: Observed At
observed_at.description: When this quote was last seen individually at the source, in RFC 3339 UTC, or `null` when not recorded.

delisted_at.title: Delisted At
delisted_at.description: When the item was found to be no longer listed on this side of the market, in RFC 3339 UTC, or `null` while it is listed. A delisted quote keeps its last price, with `quantity` `0`.

fresh_at.title: Fresh At
fresh_at.description: When this quote was last confirmed current by the source, in RFC 3339 UTC: the latest of `changed_at`, `observed_at` and the completion of the last full scan of this market.

step_index.description: Zero-based index of the offending step; omitted for chain-level issues.

is_two_sided.title: Is Two Sided

ask_amount.title: Ask Amount

bid_amount.title: Bid Amount
